close_reason: Fixed in next commit. memory.rs:817 Email::deserialize failure path now hits a debug_assert! (dev/CI surfacing) before returning None. Release build behaviour unchanged. Picked the debug_assert mitigation from the bead's three options because this is a reference impl: the assert catches fixture drift / type evolution in CI, and the comment on the assert points future production-backend contributors at the failure mode they need to propagate via their own MemoryError-equivalent. cargo test, clippy, fmt all clean.
description:
src/memory.rs line 740: 'let email: Email = Email::deserialize(val).ok()?' inside the filter loop silently drops any email whose stored JSON fails to deserialize. The .ok()? converts a deserialize error into 'skip this entry' with no logging, no metric, no test signal.

Low probability of triggering today (the backend writes typed objects and only reads them back), but a real failure mode if:
- A future jmap-mail-types Email change makes an old stored value fail to deserialize (forward-compat hole)
- A test backend is seeded by direct JSON insertion that drifts from the current Email shape
- Manual corruption of test fixtures

In all three cases, the corrupted email vanishes from query results silently. A user (or test author) sees fewer hits than expected with no error to diagnose.

Mitigation options:
- Propagate the error via the MemoryError type and surface it as a backend Error
- Add a debug_assert! that hits on .err() so test failures surface in CI
- Add a single eprintln! gated by feature='memory-trace'

Reference impl so the bar is lower than production; flagged here so a future contributor copying this pattern into a production backend knows the failure mode.
title: Email::deserialize failures in memory.rs query silently drop entries from result
